defect_reasons.insufficient_boundary_condition: With T6222 ('A 4.5 cm layer ... was plated onto the second sphere') the text never says whether the present-tense stated radius of 10 cm is the radius before or after the completed plating; the reading that it already includes the layer gives 12.44 kW, not the certified 26.16 kW.
defect_reasons.other: A 4.5 cm (and up to 7.5 cm) 'plated layer' is physically implausible for plating, making the R sentences artificial.

counterexamples: T6222 read as: the sphere 'has a radius of 10 cm' now, after a layer 'was plated' onto it earlier, so r2 = 10 cm and P2 = 12.4416 kW, contradicting the certified 26.1585 kW.
notes: Arithmetic verified: base 12.4416 kW; r2 = 12.5 cm -> 19.44 kW; 14.5 cm -> 26.1585 kW; 17.5 cm -> 38.1024 kW; all D answers 12.4416 kW. The authors' own d_kind_note concedes that a layer plated on the second sphere earlier 'is still on it', which is exactly why the past-tense T6222 is ambiguous: the base problem gives the sphere's radius in the present tense, so a completed plating may already be included in it. For present-tense TA4B6 the additive reading is natural and I accept R 26.16 kW. In pass 1 I flagged this as medium; on reflection, because it yields materially different answers for a certified R sentence, it falls under the admission rule for a missing deciding condition, so I raise it to high here (pass 1 unchanged). Minimal pairs TCB5F/TA4B6 and T4B8C/T6222 keep 4.5 cm and differ only in attachment (bracket/disc vs sphere); T298E and TDB9C are declared numeral-free controls.
